paper.title: MobileSteward: Integrating Multiple App-Oriented Agents with Self-Evolution to Automate Cross-App Instructions

gap.author_gap: Procedure-oriented/single mobile agents fail on cross-app instructions: complex task relationships, diverse app environments, error propagation and information loss; MobileAgent-v2 is a static framework without experience accumulation.
gap.checked_gap: The multi-agent decomposition gap is plausible and supported by baseline SR near 0 on CAPBench; the retained-component gap (static -> self-evolving memory) is thin: it is stated as an analogy to a steward gaining familiarity, not as a measured failure of static memory.
lineage: AppAgent (exploration/demo-generated element docs) -> MobileAgent / MobileAgent-v2 (planning/decision/reflection agents + memory unit) -> MobileSteward (app-oriented agents + evolving expertise/guideline memory)
Experience-memory neighbors named but not compared as evolving systems: MobileGPT hierarchical app memory, AutoDroid UTG memory (AutoDroid run only as a baseline)
gap.closest_adjacent: MobileAgent-v2 and AutoDroid/MobileGPT experience memories, as characterized in this paper's Related Work (original texts not in the pinned input package)
gap.residue: Cross-app tasks need scheduling and information hand-off; static per-app prompts cannot adapt to app-specific tricks.
gap.stakes: Success rate on CAPBench of baselines 0.00-0.21 vs 0.55-0.59.
gap.method_response: Per-app agents with retrievable successful-task guidelines and Steward-held app expertise; reflection and info passing between agents.
gap.remaining_gap: No evidence that the memory (not extra retries/steps/prompt structure) closes the evolving-memory gap beyond +0.05 SR; no comparison against another experience-memory scheme; deployment without trusted success signal untested.
